stories.new_fact: AP reported Trump said he would ban CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House over coverage, while reporters from those outlets remained on the grounds Friday afternoon and enforcement details were unclear.
stories.new_takeaway: The story becomes concrete only if the threat turns into credential enforcement, pool exclusion, a gate denial or court action.
stories.why_now: The statement was made September 18 and was published in current AP coverage before the September 19 episode.
stories.previous_coverage: The prior week focused on FEMA staffing, mail voting, elections, Fed and data centers; no recent full segment covered press credentials or White House access.
stories.uncertainty: The White House had not detailed enforcement mechanics at the time of reporting.
stories.watch: Watch for written credential rules, pool exclusion, Secret Service gate denials or emergency court filings.

stories.new_fact: Axios Columbus reported three more Central Ohio beer brands or locations recently dropped off the map and connected that to national craft production declines and local cost pressures.
stories.new_takeaway: A local identity and tourism story is becoming a small-business margin and vacancy story as drink preferences and costs move against taprooms.
stories.why_now: The Axios story was published September 18 during Oktoberfest season and after another set of closures.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent local segments covered data-center guardrails, Hilliard parkland, OSU speech rules, Italian Village housing and school report cards; this is a different local business beat.
stories.uncertainty: It is unclear whether closures accelerate after seasonal traffic or whether stronger local brands stabilize.
stories.watch: Watch closures after Oktoberfest and whether breweries shift into food, events, distribution, THC drinks or nonalcoholic products.

stories.new_fact: MGIC increased temporary maximum loan amounts for MGIC Go loans effective immediately, including 850,000 dollars for one-unit properties and 1,634,950 dollars for four-unit properties, with higher Alaska and Hawaii ceilings.
stories.new_takeaway: Loan teams get a near-conforming MI routing option for some files above current GSE limits if AUS acceptance and loan-amount-only ineligibility conditions are met.
stories.why_now: MGIC issued Underwriting Bulletin 04-2026 on September 18, superseding Bulletin 02-2026 from September 11.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent lending segments covered Freddie PMMS, Fannie MI termination, active-purchase rate triage and VantageScore; this is a distinct MI eligibility/routing update.
stories.uncertainty: Other MGIC Go guidelines, AUS responses and investor overlays can still block the file; other MIs may or may not match.
stories.watch: Watch whether other mortgage insurers match MGIC's temporary loan-limit increase and whether investors accept those files without overlays.
stories.workflow: MI eligibility and loan-routing workflow for above-current-conforming loan amounts that are otherwise AUS-acceptable.

stories.new_fact: The Wall Street Journal reported Mastercard rolled out an AI payment option with Alchemy that can issue a restricted virtual card to a user's AI agent for online purchases.
stories.new_takeaway: Issuer control design shifts from a human click to proving the customer's delegated intent, limits and liability when software buys on the customer's behalf.
stories.why_now: The Journal reported the rollout September 18, following the Thursday announcement.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent AI in Banking segments covered JPMorgan coding controls, Zopa transaction assistant, Goldman bankers, Schwab advisors, Pockit support, Rogo and FIS; this rotates to payments and authorization.
stories.uncertainty: No adoption, mistaken-purchase, fraud-loss, dispute-volume or issuer-support metric was disclosed.
stories.watch: Watch for issuer participation, agentic-token details and dispute data after real customers use the tool.
stories.ledger_row_changed: Added Mastercard / Alchemy | lanes 1 and 8 | announced | agentic-commerce payment option using restricted virtual cards for AI agents; evidence rank reputable reporting; no outcome metrics disclosed.

stories.new_fact: AP reported Xi Jinping will make a U.S. state visit next week and that the agenda includes artificial intelligence, tariffs, rare earths and strategic trade issues.
stories.new_takeaway: Frontier AI availability is constrained by diplomacy and export-control channels as much as by benchmark progress.
stories.why_now: AP published the state-visit agenda September 19 and the meeting is next week.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent frontier segments covered Anthropic R&D metrics, OpenAI misalignment reporting, embedded evaluators, China model competition and U.S.-China AI safety disagreements; this adds the dated state-visit venue and access-policy watch.
stories.uncertainty: No binding AI agreement, export-control change or safety process has been announced.
stories.watch: Watch whether the visit produces AI export-control, chip, rare-earth or safety language specific enough to affect labs and enterprise providers.
stories.frontier_bar: Policy that binds labs directly or changes access; this is a diplomatic agenda/access item, not a model capability benchmark.

stories.new_fact: AP's Friday market table reported the S&P 500 up 0.2%, Nasdaq up 0.4%, Dow down 0.2%, Russell 2000 down 0.5%, and the 10-year Treasury yield near 5%.
stories.new_takeaway: Technology strength is cushioning the index while yields keep pressure on small caps, mortgage pricing and refinancing assumptions.
stories.why_now: The market move was Friday's close before the Saturday episode.
stories.previous_coverage: Markets were covered daily, but this is a compact current close rather than a repeated Fed segment.
stories.uncertainty: Weekend oil and bond-market developments can change Monday pricing.
stories.watch: Watch whether the 10-year stays near 5% and whether market breadth weakens beneath AI-linked leadership.

stories.new_fact: Forecast sources indicated Columbus highs around 79 to 81 for Saturday, near 80 Sunday and upper 60s Monday, with rain risk in the period.
stories.new_takeaway: Outdoor plans are workable but need radar checks, and Monday may be the more disruptive commute setup.
stories.why_now: Weather is included for same-day and near-term planning.
stories.previous_coverage: Routine weather appears daily; this is current planning only.
stories.uncertainty: Rain timing can shift by neighborhood and forecast update.
stories.watch: Recheck radar before Saturday outdoor plans and Monday commute timing.
